terms.meaning: one unit of stored text space; some characters take more than one byte

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Password length constant
sections.what: Sets the minimum password length to 10 characters.
sections.why: Likely reason: one constant keeps the rule and its message in step.

sections.name: passwordPolicy
sections.title: Password rule
sections.what: Requires at least 10 and at most 128 characters, each with a message.
sections.why: Likely reason: a minimum for strength and a maximum to limit very large inputs.
sections.watch_out: The hashing method ignores everything past 72 bytes, a known property of bcrypt, so characters past that point add no protection.

sections.name: registerInput, RegisterInput
sections.title: Sign-up form rules
sections.what: Describes the sign-up form: the name must be 1 to 60 characters, the email is trimmed, lowercased and checked, the password must meet the rule, and the age box must be ticked.
sections.why: Likely reason: checks input before any database work, with a clear message for each problem.
sections.watch_out: The age check requires exactly true, so an unticked box is refused with a message about the 18 and over rule.

summary: Defines the password rule and the sign-up form rules.
purpose: Input checks for creating an account.
why: Likely reason: one set of rules keeps the form messages and the server checks in step.
how: 1. Set the minimum password length. 2. Build the password rule with messages. 3. Build the sign-up form rule, including the age tick.
outputs: Cleaned data, or messages explaining what to fix.
risks: The hashing method only uses the first 72 bytes of a password, but the rule allows up to 128 characters, so extra characters add no strength.
debug: If valid sign-ups are refused, check trimming, the email check and the password length.
